rationale: This is a mechanical ensemble of the archive's two best-performing signals rather than a new mechanism, and the two legs overlap substantially (both are cash-flow-versus-investment constructs, with the acquisition leg already paired with an oancf-based profitability rank), so the archive's own SUMRANK precedent (self_funding_plus_investment_payoff, alpha diluted to 0.029/t 1.96) predicts averaging-down rather than incremental insight.

Re-deflating cumulative acquisitions by the firm's own cumulative organic investment instead of assets is a substantive composition-versus-scale test with a clear diagnostic payoff either way, though it remains a deflator refinement of an already-successful archive signal and the depreciation-floored denominator will behave erratically for asset-light acquirers.

The COALESCE-to-zero plus MAX(.,dp) construction means the majority of firms with little or no goodwill are scored purely by oancf/dp, so the signal is a mixture of a cash-flow-to-depreciation profitability ratio (which will dominate the long leg) and a goodwill-intensity ratio, making the computed quantity inconsistent with the stated stale-acquisition-premium hypothesis and confounded with the known goodwill-to-assets anomaly.

The diagnosis is legitimate and specific — an after-depreciation earnings numerator is mechanically depressed by the same capex sitting in the denominator — and substituting operating cash flow breaks that link while retaining the depreciation-floored cumulative denominator, making this a mechanism-driven fix rather than a horizon or scaling tweak.

The transition dimension of this exact ratio was already tested and failed in the archive (own_history_position_of_funding_coverage), and a raw first difference of an unbounded, depreciation-floored ratio is scale-dependent and dominated by transitory capex/cash-flow noise, so the discretization diagnosis is plausible but not enough to make this substantively different rather than a re-transformation of a failed construct.

Benchmarking five-year cumulative capex against five-year cumulative depreciation is an economically meaningful replacement-rate standard that is distinct from both the own-mean norm and the cross-sectional asset-growth channel already tested, and the null and positive outcomes carry different, informative interpretations — though the sub-replacement leg will be correlated with the classic investment/CMA factor and the profitability-minus-investment rank-difference form has repeatedly produced weak FF5 alphas in this archive.
